title: Bait Works Well
body: This trap replaces an Oak Stump brand yellowjacket trap that finally broke during a storm. Oak Trap isn't made any longer, but I prefer the shape of their trap (much larger -- at least 6" in diameter), and it seemed to attract more wasps and yellowjackets. However, this trap does work. The bait also works well, but is expensive to replace. Homemade solution can also be used.

title: Best Bait/Trap Ever.
body: I used two of these on a hunting trip last week where we were inundated with yellow jackets. The first clue to how effective this would be was when one of my friends snipped open a corner of the cellophane pouch that the bait was in and he was mobbed with yellow jackets before he could pour it into the trap. The traps would fill up 3/4 of the way in just a couple of hours. I have probably 4 or 5 different brands of yellow jacket traps and this one is by far the most effective ones I've ever used. I am so impressed that I bought more of the BioCare bait to use in my other brands of traps as well. I did not purchase this from Amazon because I was a long ways from home and needed it right away so I bought them at a hardware store in the nearest town. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this trap to anyone with a yellow jacket issue.

title: Yellow Jackets Be Gone!
body: This is a very effective product! While I recognize that wasps are beneficial for killing garden pests and generally leave them to do their thing, this year they would not leave the monarch larvae on my milkweed alone. They killed at least seven of them in one afternoon and I resorted to mosquito netting and this product to protect the rest. I put it out 3 days ago and there are already at least a dozen dead wasps in it. I plan to set out more milkweed for the 4th generation egg lay in September/October and just ordered more bait to see me through into fall. So, if you're looking for a non-toxic, refillable, and reasonably priced way to practice wasp control, I don't think you can do much better than BioCare.
